findings.reason: parser.ts:1452 only does state.position++, while the removed skipByteOrderMark also set lineStart. As a result parseNode at :1243 computes blockIndent=1, readBlockSequence at :992 breaks when the next line has lineIndent 0, and readDocument at :1421 throws. skipSeparationSpace at :336 sees position!==lineStart and FEFF is not whitespace, so '#' is not treated as a comment, and the '...' check at :1388 also needs position===lineStart.
findings.claim: The leading BOM is now skipped without setting lineStart, so the first line's indent and line-start checks are off. Multi-line top-level block collections, a comment right after the BOM, and a '...' right after the BOM all misparse.
findings.evidence: The new line `if (state.input.charCodeAt(state.position) === 0xFEFF) state.position++` leaves `state.lineStart` at 0. The removed skipByteOrderMark also set `state.lineStart = state.position`. parseNode then computes `const blockIndent = state.position - state.lineStart` (line 1243), which gives 1 for the first top-level node. readBlockSequence stops at `if (state.lineIndent < nodeIndent ...) break` (line 992) when the second line has lineIndent 0, and readDocument then throws 'end of the stream or a document separator is expected' (lines 1419-1422). The only BOM unit test, test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs:7, uses a single-line mapping ('﻿foo: bar\n'), so it never reaches this path.

findings.reason: The diff deletes testDocumentBoundary and the per-document skipByteOrderMark. The checks at :672, :776 and :1421 now call bare testDocumentSeparator, and BOM skipping happens only once at position 0 (:1452). So 'a\n﻿---\nb' is read as one scalar where the baseline split it into two documents.
findings.claim: BOMs at the start of later documents in a multi-document stream are no longer accepted. A BOM-prefixed '---' no longer ends the previous scalar or document.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes the per-document `skipByteOrderMark(state)` call from the parseEvents loop and deletes testDocumentBoundary, which looked for a BOM-prefixed '---'/'%' boundary. The block-scalar (line 672), plain-scalar (line 776) and readDocument (line 1421) boundary checks now call bare `testDocumentSeparator`, so a BOM before a separator no longer ends the scalar or document. Only the single leading BOM at position 0 is still skipped (line 1452). The spec suite maps '⇔' to '﻿' (test/spec/spec.test.mjs:52), so this feature is part of the conformance surface. The yaml-test-suite fixtures are not in the export, so I could not run them.

findings.claim: The diff removes deliberate BOM-boundary support with no test and no record that the removal was asked for.
findings.evidence: Lines 9-36 of diff.patch delete skipByteOrderMark and testDocumentBoundary, including the comments 'Fast path: most document boundaries do not have a BOM' and 'BOM-prefixed boundaries are rare'. acceptance.md says only 'story.md is the spec', and no story.md exists in the packet or export. The diff changes no test file.

findings.reason: A grep of test/ finds only load-other.test.mjs:7 (load('﻿foo: bar\n')) as a core BOM parse assertion. A single-line mapping parses even with blockIndent=1, so this test passes despite the C1/X1 bug. This is a coverage gap, not a defect in the change itself.
findings.claim: The only BOM load test uses a single-line input, so it can't catch the multi-line and multi-document regressions.
findings.evidence: `assert.deepStrictEqual(load('﻿foo: bar\n'), { foo: 'bar' })` is the only BOM parse assertion in test/core. No test loads a BOM followed by a multi-line block collection, or a BOM after a '...' or '---' separator.
